Chapter 29: Systems Memory Freedom & Raw Pointers

Cluster-lang is designed to replace both Python and C/C++/Rust. While high-level application code enjoys strict automatic memory safety and bounds checking, systems programming, game engines, embedded drivers, and OS kernels require direct hardware memory control.

Cluster-lang provides Systems Memory Freedom: safe, high-level ergonomics by default, with opt-in zero-overhead raw pointer manipulation.

This chapter covers:

1. The unsafe Block Boundary for auditing low-level operations.

2. Raw Pointer Types (ptr, ptr[T], T).

3. Address-of (& / addr_of) and Dereferencing ( / deref).

4. Direct Heap Allocations (mem_alloc, mem_free, mem_realloc).

5. Memory Block Manipulation (mem_copy, mem_set, mem_move).

6. Pointer Arithmetic (ptr_add, ptr_diff, ptr_to_int, int_to_ptr).

7. The High-Performance Arena Allocator (std::alloc).

1. The unsafe Block Boundary

To maintain software reliability, raw pointer dereferences and unchecked memory modifications can be scoped inside explicit unsafe blocks. This allows developers and security auditors to quickly isolate bare-metal operations:

fn main():
    val := 100

    unsafe:
        # Explicitly marked low-level memory block
        p := addr_of(val)
        put "Address of val: " + to_text(ptr_to_int(p))

2. Address-of and Dereferencing

Cluster-lang allows retrieving the memory address of local variables, model fields, and vector elements:

fn main():
    target := 42

    # Take address using addr_of or &
    p := addr_of(target)

    # Read value through pointer (dereference)
    v := *p
    put "Read through pointer: " + to_text(v)   # 42

    # Mutate value through pointer
    *p = 999
    put "Mutated target: " + to_text(target)    # 999

3. Direct Heap Allocation Primitives

For performance-critical code where the general garbage collector or automatic lifetime manager is bypassed, developers can manage raw heap memory directly:

  • mem_alloc(bytes: int) -> ptr: Allocates a raw byte buffer on the heap (maps to libc malloc).
  • mem_free(p: ptr): Releases the allocated block (maps to libc free).
  • mem_realloc(p: ptr, new_bytes: int) -> ptr: Resizes an existing heap allocation.
fn main():
    # Allocate a buffer for 10 64-bit integers (80 bytes)
    buffer := mem_alloc(80)

    # Store values at offsets
    p0 := ptr_add(buffer, 0)
    *p0 = 12345

    put "Value at buffer[0]: " + to_text(*p0)

    # Always free manually allocated buffers
    mem_free(buffer)

4. Block Memory Operations (mem_set, mem_copy, mem_move)

Bulk memory transfers compile directly to SIMD-accelerated CPU instructions:

  • mem_set(dest: ptr, byte_val: int, count: int): Sets memory to a specified byte value (e.g. zeroing buffers).
  • mem_copy(dest: ptr, src: ptr, count: int): High-speed non-overlapping copy.
  • mem_move(dest: ptr, src: ptr, count: int): Safe copy handling overlapping regions.
fn main():
    src := mem_alloc(64)
    dst := mem_alloc(64)

    # Initialize source to zeros
    mem_set(src, 0, 64)

    # Copy 64 bytes from src to dst
    mem_copy(dst, src, 64)

    mem_free(src)
    mem_free(dst)

5. Pointer Arithmetic

Cluster-lang supports precise byte-level and element-level pointer offset calculations:

  • ptr_add(p: ptr, offset_bytes: int) -> ptr: Returns a new pointer offset by the given bytes.
  • ptr_diff(p1: ptr, p2: ptr) -> int: Returns the byte difference between two addresses.
  • ptr_to_int(p: ptr) -> int: Casts an address to a 64-bit unsigned integer.
  • int_to_ptr(addr: int) -> ptr: Reconstructs a pointer from an integer address (e.g. for memory-mapped I/O).

6. Scoped Arena Allocator (std::alloc)

Repeated individual heap allocations cause memory fragmentation and cache misses. The Cluster standard library includes a high-performance Arena Allocator in std/alloc.zk (std/alloc.cl):

# Create an arena with a 1MB contiguous buffer
arena := Arena_new(1048576)

# Allocate fast, linear memory slices with zero malloc overhead
buf1 := Arena_alloc(arena, 256)
buf2 := Arena_alloc(arena, 512)

# Reset or release all allocations at once in a single instruction!
Arena_reset(arena)
Arena_free(arena)
